title: Six Mornings on the Estuary
intro: No argument, no conclusion — just the light, the tide and the people who count birds before breakfast.

add_image.image_alt: Mist over an estuary at dawn
add_image.image_caption: 06:12. The tide is still out; the mud is doing the talking.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: The estuary is a working surface. Every low tide exposes a new version of it — channels shifted, a log arrived, a footprint that was not there yesterday.

images.image_alt: Sampling gear set up at the waterline
images.image_caption: 06:52. The pump is set up before the tide turns.
07:05. The first sample, before the wind picks up.
07:30. The channel catches the light and briefly looks solid.
08:00. The survey team, arriving late and apologising.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: Six mornings is not a dataset. It is a habit — the kind that makes a place familiar enough to notice when it changes.
